witness.n_range: 0 <= n <= p + ceil(p^c) inclusive, per (p, c)
witness.property: for each (p, c, n): exists integers a, b with n < a < p^c, n < b < p^c and (a*b) mod p == 1
witness.expected: verify(witness) returns True with zero counterexamples; raises on any failure

claim: Exact fail-closed integer verification: verify(witness) exhaustively checks, with exact integer arithmetic only (no floats, no I/O, no network, no filesystem), that for every prime 3<=p<=43, every c in {3/5,3/4,1,3/2}, and every 0<=n<=p+ceil(p^c), there exist a,b in the strict interval (n, n+p^c) with ab≡1 mod p. Any failure raises; True is returned only on zero counterexamples — the full enumerated scope of L1. Scope: finite enumerated domain only; general-p scaling remains analytic.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
